body:
| 👮 **Wachiman** | Card that is still up is never hidden before the next screenshot or recording |
|:--|:--|
| **Priority** | **Should** · a change is expected; answer if you disagree |
| **Severity** | 🟠 Fix |
| **Area** | 🐛 bug |
| **Confidence** | 🟥🟥⬜ Medium |
| **Track record** | no record yet · seed |

Content protection is the only thing keeping the card out of later captures. The capture toast this copies treats content protection as the *second* guard: `capture-toast-window.ts:305` says "Second guard behind `beforeCapture` dismissing it", and `index.ts:670` wires `dismissToast` into `captureWindowHooks`. The ready window is never hooked in. Nothing in `index.ts` or the hub calls `recordingReady.close()` before a screenshot or when a take starts. The card has no timer and stays up until the user acts, so it is often still on screen when the next capture begins.

On Windows builds before 10 2004, the repo itself notes that content protection "paints the window black in captures instead of leaving it out" (`area-geometry.ts:82-85`). There, a card left up shows as a black 452×~320 block in the next whole-display recording or screenshot, and nothing tells the user. On every platform it also stays over the display being recorded through the next countdown and take.

Fix: close the card from `captureWindowHooks` (next to `dismissToast`) and on `recordingStart` or the start request, or document why it should stay.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

| 👮 **Wachiman** | A re-shown window can flash the previous take's card |
|:--|:--|
| **Priority** | **Could** · worth a look; change on the merits |
| **Severity** | 🟡 Consider |
| **Area** | 🐛 bug |
| **Confidence** | 🟥🟥⬜ Medium |
| **Track record** | no record yet · seed |

`close()` only hides the window. The card renderer keeps the old payload rendered, and `cardHeight` keeps the old height. On the next `show()`, `present()` sends the new payload and immediately calls `showInactive()`. The window can therefore show its last composited frame (the previous recording's duration and size, at the old height) before React repaints with the new payload. Consider clearing the card when it is hidden (for example, sending a null payload on close), or showing the window only after the card has painted (for example, on its next resize/ack).

<!-- wachi:finding -->

| 👮 **Wachiman** | \`recording-ready:show\` accepts any sender |
|:--|:--|
| **Priority** | **Could** · worth a look; change on the merits |
| **Severity** | 🟡 Consider |
| **Area** | 🔐 security |
| **Confidence** | 🟥🟥⬜ Medium |
| **Track record** | no record yet · seed |

The card's own channels check `isOwnSender`, but the `recordingReadyShow` handler accepts an invoke from any webContents that loads the preload. That includes the card window itself, the capture toast and the panels. Any of them can pop the always-on-top card with an arbitrary assetId, which a later Open/Edit then navigates the main window to. Consider limiting this handler to the main window's webContents.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

| 👮 **Wachiman** | Pressing Back to the fresh recording's page floats the desktop card again |
|:--|:--|
| **Priority** | **Could** · worth a look; change on the merits |
| **Severity** | 🟡 Consider |
| **Area** | 🐛 bug |
| **Confidence** | 🟥🟥⬜ Medium |
| **Track record** | no record yet · seed |

`useFloatingReadyCard` only remembers that it already asked in a ref (`use-floating-ready-card.ts:18`). The ref is lost when the page unmounts. Here is the sequence: a chip or Edit first on the floating card navigates the main window to Prepare or the editor (`recording-ready-window.ts:166-172`), and the user presses Back. The page remounts under the same history entry, so `location.state.fromRecording` and `location.key` are unchanged. `showCard` is true again, the ref is empty, and `showRecordingReady` is called a second time. Main does not check whether it already showed this asset (`recording-ready-window.ts:134-147`), so the always-on-top window opens again over whatever the user is doing. The old in-app card had the same remount gap, because `cardDismissedFor` is component state. Before this change it reappeared inside the page; now it reappears on the desktop. The backlog doc also says "the card never shows twice" (`floating-ready-window.md:51`), which this sequence contradicts. One fix: record per `location.key` that the card was asked for, somewhere that survives a remount (module scope, or `navigate(..., { replace: true, state })` clearing `fromRecording`). Another: have main skip a payload whose `assetId` it has already shown.

<!-- wachi:finding -->
